newsitem.title: JAPAN: Marubeni, Teijin set up textile venture in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Marubeni, Teijin set up textile venture in U.S.

text.p: Japanese trading house Marubeni Corp, a U.S. subsidiary and Teijin Ltd have set up a joint venture in the United States to dye textiles, Marubeni Corp said on Thursday.
The joint venture, Wateree Textile Corp, is capitalised at $6 million and headquartered in South Carolina, Marubeni Crop said in a statement.
Marubeni America Corp holds 80 percent in the textile dyeing firm, while Marbubeni Corp and Teijin each own 10 percent, the statement said.
The companies are investing a total of $21 million in the joint venture, it said.
The new factory, which is expected to start operating in the second quarter of 1998, will have a capacity to dye 2.5 million metres of polyester taffeta per month.
The joint venture aims for annual revenues of $9.75 million in 2000, the statement said.
